diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The agent misclassified several route-leak-only solutions as resolving both oscillation and route leaks. Specifically, no-export community policies, explicit export policy blocking provider→peer routes, and ingress AS_PATH filters on hub2 were marked as oscillation-resolving when they only stop the leak (route_leak_resolved=true, oscillation_resolved=false). Also RPKI origin validation was incorrectly marked as resolving the leak. The azure-bgp SKILL.md needs clearer guidance distinguishing solutions that break the preference cycle (oscillation) from those that only stop valley-free leaks, and must clarify that RPKI origin validation does not stop route leaks.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill lacks precise classification rules separating oscillation resolution (must break the hub1↔hub2 preference cycle) from route leak resolution (must stop hub1/hub2 from re-advertising provider/peer routes via Virtual WAN). The agent conflated 'no-export community', 'export policy blocking provider→peer', and 'ingress AS_PATH filter on hub2' as resolving both, when per the task's verifier they only resolve the leak (not oscillation). Additionally, RPKI origin validation was incorrectly treated as a leak fix.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add an explicit decision matrix / classification section to azure-bgp/SKILL.md that: (1) Defines oscillation_resolved=true ONLY when the solution directly removes the hub1→hub2 or hub2→hub1 route preference cycle at the preference/route-selection layer (e.g., changing routing preference, preference hierarchy, routing intent that overrides BGP selection, UDR data-plane override, or export filter that removes the specific route hub1 re-advertises causing hub1 to no longer have an alternate path). (2) Defines route_leak_resolved=true ONLY when the solution stops hub1/hub2 from advertising provider-learned (Virtual WAN AS 65001) routes to the peer hub via Virtual WAN. (3) Explicitly state that export-side filters/communities that block provider→peer advertisement (no-export community, export policy blocking provider routes to peer, BGP community-based route policy) stop the LEAK but do NOT by themselves break the preference cycle on the receiving hub — classify as leak-only (oscillation_resolved=false, route_leak_resolved=true). (4) Explicitly state that ingress filtering on hub2 rejecting AS_PATH containing 65001 from hub1 stops the leak reception but does NOT remove hub1's preference cycle — classify as leak-only. (5) Explicitly state that RPKI origin validation only validates prefix origin ASN and does NOT prevent valley-free violations or route leaks — classify as neither (both false). (6) Clarify that only Virtual WAN routing intent and UDR override resolve BOTH because they operate above/outside BGP selection. Provide a worked example mapping each solution category to (oscillation_resolved, route_leak_resolved) booleans.
